paper.title: Optimal Design for Reward Modeling in RLHF

settings.name_in_paper: Offline linear contextual dueling bandit for reward modeling (Bradley-Terry), simple regret
unmapped: Offline/non-adaptive design: all T query pairs are selected before any feedback is observed
Simple regret is the worst case over N given action sets A_n (pairs compared only within the same set), arbitrary (non-i.i.d.) action sets
Logistic (Bradley-Terry) link on differences of embeddings, linear reward in a known feature map
settings.definition_quote: The preference feedback is then received as \{\al_t \succ \am_t\} with probability \sigma(\langle \theta^\star, \al_t - \am_t \rangle) ... \regret_{\alg}(T, (\cA_n)_{n \in [N]}, \theta^\star) = \max_{n \in [N]}\max_{a \in \cA_n} \ps{\theta^\star}{a- \hat{a}_T(\cA_n)}. Assumption: For any x,y, \psi(x,y) \in \oball(0,1)... \theta^\star \in \oball(0,1).

settings.name_in_paper: Changing action set (online) dueling selection, simple regret (lower bound)
unmapped: At each step a new action set A_t arrives and the learner must pick a pair from it; simple regret is the max over all steps' action sets
settings.definition_quote: Formally, at each step t \in [T], an action set \cA_t, t \in [T] is provided and the algorithm must select a pair of samples (\al_t, \am_t) \in \cA_t^2.

conditions: actions and theta^star in the unit ball (H1)
tuning: samples drawn according to a (1+eps_alg)-approximation of the optimal design

source.label: theorem:simple_regret_upper_bound
source.quote: Let $\epsilon >0$ and suppose that we collect at least $T\geq d^2$ samples according to an $(1+\epsilon)$ approximation $\hat{\pi}$ of the optimal design policy $\pi^\star$ for the problem. Then, for any $\cB$ and $\theta^\star \in \oball(0,1)$, with probability at least $1-\delta$, ... \regret \leq 20 (1+\epsilon)\, \sqrt{d/T} [\sqrt{2 \log (1/\delta) + d\, \log(\lambda^{1-1/d}+4T/d\lambda^{1/d} )} + \sqrt{\lambda} ]

results.notes: Interpreted 4T/dλ^{1/d} as 4T/(d λ^{1/d}) per the proof. Simple regret is a max over all given action sets.

conditions: actions and theta^star in the unit ball (H1)

source.label: corollary:simple_regret_upper_bound
source.quote: Suppose that we have selected the samples $\dselect$ to label under $\hat{\pi}$, a $3/2$-approximation of the optimal design policy $\pi^\star$. Choosing $\lambda = 1/d$ for the regularization, for any $\delta \in (0,1)$, ... with probability at least $1-\delta$, \regret \leq 30\sqrt{d/T} \times [\sqrt{2 \log(1/\delta) + d\log((1+4T)/d^{1-1/d})}+1/\sqrt{d} ]

conditions: actions and theta^star in the unit ball (H1)

source.label: corollary:simple_regret_upper_bound
source.quote: and as a consequence, choosing $\delta = d^{1-1/d}/(4T+1)$, we can bound the expectation of the regret as \E[\regret] \leq 30 \frac{d+2}{\sqrt{T}}\sqrt{\log(\frac{4T+1}{d^{1-1/d}})} + 31/\sqrt{T}

conditions: hard instance: theta in {±sqrt(d/T)}^d, action set [-1/sqrt(d),1/sqrt(d)]^d

source.label: theorem:lower_bound
source.quote: Suppose that $d \geq 16$ and that $T \geq d^2$. For any algorithm $\alg$ which samples $T$ pairs from $\cB$ and receives a preference feedback before outputing an action $\hat{a}(\cA_n) \in \cA_n$ for an input $\cA_n$, there exists $(\cA_n)_{n \in [N]} \subseteq \oball(0,1)$ as well as $\theta^\star \in \oball(0,1)$ such that \regret(T, (\cA_n)_{n \in [N]}, \theta^\star) \geq d \, \rme^{-5}/4\sqrt{T}.

results.notes: Statement written for regret without expectation, but the proof lower-bounds the expected simple regret. Holds for any (possibly adaptive) algorithm sampling T pairs.

symbols.c_lb: positive constant independent of T and d (bounds the KL of the single informative round)

conditions: adversarially chosen action sets: A_1..A_{T-1}={±e_1}, A_T={±e_2}

source.label: lemma:lower_bound_online
source.quote: Consider the $2$-dimensional euclidian space Span$(e_1, e_2)$ as the whole action space. In that case, there exists a set of actions $(\cA_t)_{t \in [T]}$ and some $\theta^\star \in \oball(0,1)$ such the regret defined in \eqref{equation:definition_online_regret} for any algorithm $\alg$ satisfies \regret_\alg(T, (\cA_t)_{t \in [T]}, \theta^\star) \geq \rme^{-c}/2, for some $c >0$ independent of $T$ and $d$.

results.notes: Constant (non-vanishing) simple regret lower bound with changing adversarial action sets; proof is in terms of probability of a wrong output, so treated as expected regret.
